Here's the background information if you never heard of the Minamata disease.

After the Korean War, Japan entered the period of high speed growth (which some describe to be a miracle, but really a combination of factors that lead to immense, sustained growth of the Japanese economy until the burst of the bubble in the 1980s. However, that period of growth didn’t come without sacrifices. There was heavy pollution from the rapid industrialization that occurred. And, unfortunately, many were victims of industrial diseases caused by industrial waste. There were four big pollution diseases in Japan – Minamata disease being one of them. One of the other diseases, one of the earliest discovered even before the period of high-speed growth, was the Itai-Itai disease. “Itai” means “it hurts”, a phrase victims would often call out. (There are many pictures of victims since these diseases attracted media attention at the time. Personally, I find some very painful to look at.)

The Minamata disease was caused by mercury. “Symptoms include ataxia, numbness in the hands and feet, general muscle weakness, loss of peripheral vision, and damage to hearing and speech.”

However, action was taken against pollution after these diseases were covered strongly by the media. Activists took action, lawsuits occurred, and the government intervened. These diseases declined strongly after the 1970s.
